scope: Modern Kannada grammar and writing-quality rule catalogue
note: Kannada grammar is extensive and varies by literary/spoken register. These categories provide an extensible rule base; they are not a claim that every possible grammatical construction can be reduced to deterministic rules.

sentence_structure.rule: A clause normally has one finite/conjugated verb; coordinated actions commonly use non-finite/participial forms.
Relative participles commonly precede the noun they modify.

noun_and_case.function: means, instrument, source in appropriate contexts

pronouns.rule: Pronouns distinguish person and number; third-person forms also distinguish gender in many contexts.
ಅವರು and corresponding verb agreement can express honorific reference.
ತಾನು/ತನ್ನ forms are used for reflexive reference according to syntactic context.

verb_morphology.rule: Past forms must agree with the relevant subject in person/number/gender where the construction requires agreement.
Modern Kannada non-past/progressive forms use context and auxiliary structure to distinguish meanings.
Literary Kannada has future forms that are less common in everyday spoken Kannada.
Negative constructions use appropriate negative auxiliaries/forms such as ಇಲ್ಲ, ಅಲ್ಲ, ಆಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ according to construction.
Commands use appropriate imperative forms and honorific alternatives.
Conditional/contingent constructions use appropriate participial or conditional morphology.
Causative morphology can be formed with causative suffixes such as -ಇಸು according to verb class.

agreement.rule: Finite verb forms must match the grammatical subject where agreement is expressed.
Third-person finite forms can encode masculine, feminine, neuter, or honorific/plural distinctions depending on register and construction.

nonfinite_and_auxiliaries.rule: Gerund/participial forms such as -ಇ/-ಿ can link sequential actions.
Progressive constructions commonly combine a participial form with ಇರು and the appropriate finite agreement.
Compound verb constructions combine lexical and auxiliary verbs to express aspectual or modal meaning.

sandhi_and_word_formation.rule: Adjacent vowels can change or contract at morpheme/word boundaries according to Kannada phonology.
Consonants can assimilate or change at morphological boundaries.
Final vowels of verb stems can undergo deletion or change before vowel-initial suffixes.
Compound words combine lexical elements into a single semantic unit; analysis must preserve the intended compound relation.
Distinguish Sanskrit-derived tatsama forms from adapted tadbhava forms where the lexical database provides evidence.

word_classes.rule: Names persons, places, things, concepts, or entities.
Substitutes for or refers to noun phrases.
Expresses an action, event, state, or process.
Modifies a noun; agreement and attributive forms depend on construction.
Modifies a verb, adjective, clause, or sentence; -ಆಗಿ is one productive adverbial formation.
Relationship words commonly follow their complements.

register_and_usage.rule: Keep literary (ಗ್ರಾಂಥಿಕ) and colloquial (ಗ್ರಾಮ್ಯ/ಮಾತುಕತೆ) forms distinct rather than marking one as universally incorrect.
Use respectful, complete wording for official notices, invitations, and public posters.
Use appropriate punctuation and avoid inserting spaces inside Kannada grapheme clusters.
